case_name: Shaikh Karimullah @ Babu and Others v State of Andhra Pradesh
respondent:
State of Andhra Pradesh
Supreme Court of India

6 February 2009
Criminal Appeal No. 223 of 2009 (Arising out of SLP(Crl.) No. 6657 of 2007)
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr. Arijit Pasayat, J.
Leave granted.
1.  Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court at Hyderabad dismissing the appeal filed by the appellants and two
facts: The judgment was delivered by Dr. Arijit Pasayat, J.
The appellants and two others filed an appeal against the judgment of a Division Bench of the Andhra Pradesh High Court at Hyderabad dismissing their appeal.
A-1 to A-5 were acquitted for the offence punishable under Section 148 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC').
B. Nagabhusan was a kerosene dealer and Al was having illicit intimacy with one Krupa.
On 14.1.2000 while P.Ws. 1, 3 to 6 and the deceased were performing Annadanam at Anjaneya Swamy Temple, Al kicked the Shamiana and sat on a Mahalakshmamma tree.
The prosecution version is that Al to A5 went to the temple and enquired about Krupa, and then pushed P.W.3 towards the house of Bellamkonda Venkateshwarlu abusing him.
On 31.3.2000 at about 7.30 p.m., all the accused persons armed with sticks and iron rods went to the temple and attacked P.Ws. 1, 3 to 6.
The deceased was taken to Chilakaluripet Town Police Station as the deceased was unconscious, P.W.l gave a report - Ex.P1.
On the basis of the above report, P.W. 11, the then Sub-Inspector of Police registered the case in Cr.No. 193 of 2000 and issued FIR Ex.P-10.
The trial Court by its judgment dated 9.9.2004 acquitted A1 to A5 for the offence punishable under Section 148 of the IPC.

A-2 to A-5 were found guilty for the offence under Section 302 IPC and they were sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.1000 with default stipulation, while A-4 and A-5 were not found guilty on the second charge.
A-2 to A-5 were also found not guilty for the offence under Section 324 IPC.
A4 and A5 were acquitted of all the charges.
issues: What is the appropriate conviction in this case?
Can Section 34 be pressed into service as there was no charge framed and findings recorded are contrary to the evidence?
petitioner_arguments: The judgment of the trial Court and the High Court do not suffer from any infirmity.
No charge was framed in terms of Section 34 so far as the appellant is concerned.
Except PW-1 who stated that the appellant assaulted the deceased with a stick, the other purported eye witnesses stated that the appellant had given fist blow.
The appropriate conviction would be in terms of Section 325 IPC and not Section 302 IPC.
Custodial sentence of three years would meet the ends of justice.
respondent_arguments: No infirmity in the judgments of the trial Court and the High Court.
The records clearly show that no charge was framed in terms of Section 34 so far as the appellant is concerned.
It is also accepted that except PW-1 who stated that the appellant assaulted the deceased with a stick, the other purported eye witnesses stated that the appellant had given fist blow.
court_reasoning: The trial Court by its judgment dated 9.9.2004 acquitted A1 to A5 for the offence punishable under Section 148 of the IPC.

A-2 to A-5 were found guilty for the offence under Section 302 IPC and they were sentenced to suffer imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.1000 with default stipulation, while A-4 and A-5 were not found guilty on the second charge.
The present appeal is restricted to Shaik Ibraheem (A-3), as stated by learned counsel for the appellants.
According to learned counsel for the State the judgments of the trial Court and the High Court do not suffer from any infirmity.
It is also accepted that except PW-1 who stated that the appellant assaulted the deceased with a stick, the other purported eye witnesses stated that the appellant had given fist blow.
The appropriate conviction would be in terms of Section 325 IPC and not Section 302 IPC.
Custodial sentence of three years would meet the ends of justice.
holding: The appeal is allowed to the aforesaid extent.
